Lending Rules and Small Firms

  • Ada Moss
  • Loading metrics

Figures

Abstract

Small firms borrow less when banks must hold more capital against small loans. We compare regions before and after a rule change.

Introduction

Banks price loans to small firms partly on the capital they must set aside. When that requirement rose in one region and not in its neighbour, lending to small firms in the first region fell by about a tenth.
